messages:
zoe (Docs): Heads-up: I opened PR #5233 to tighten the audit-logs export doc for SOC2 readers, add a CLI bulk-export + gzip example, and append a short Rust SDK streaming sample. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5233
rick (Security): Thanks Zoe. Two priority items: 1) public phrasing should say data is retained per the customer's retention policy and that deletions may be delayed by lawful holds and backup cycles; 2) call out that compressed exports are supported but clients should verify integrity checks.
joe (typo)
jude (Legal): Minor: prefer 'fulfilled' over 'processed' in public-facing text. Also avoid implying immediate removal from all systems. Suggest: "Redwood retains audit logs per the customer's retention policy. Export and deletion requests are fulfilled, subject to lawful holds and backup retention cycles and contractual obligations."
zoe (Docs): Good catch, Jude. I'll update the copy. Also planning to add a short CLI example that streams compressed output to disk for large exports. Draft cURL I added:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?since=2026-01-01&format=jsonl&page_size=500&compress=true" --output audit_export.jsonl.gz
```
pavan (DevEx): Nice. Add a note to verify checksums (we return a `digest` header for compressed exports). I can add Node/Python/Rust snippets for streaming.
kiyomi (Eng): Backend detail: `compress=true` sets Content-Encoding: gzip on the response and we include `X-Export-Digest: sha256:<hex>`. Also pagination uses `next_page_token` for non-stream exports; streaming mode ignores page_token but may reconnect on timeouts.
rick (Security): Add a short caveat: redaction vs purge distinction. Redaction masks PII in exported records; purge requests aim to remove records from active stores but may not affect backups immediately. For SOC2 readers, make it explicit that retention controls and holds are part of evidence.
zoe (Docs): I'll add heading: "Retention, redaction, and purge: what to expect" and include the phrase Jude suggested. Also switching TTL examples to ISO-8601 durations (e.g., P30D, P180D).
pavan (DevEx): Rust streaming example I'm adding to the PR (uses async stream):
```rust
use redwood_rs::Client;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
  let client = Client::new("$TOKEN");
  let mut stream = client.audit().export_stream("since=2026-01-01&format=jsonl&compress=true").await.unwrap();
  while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
    println!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&chunk.unwrap()));
  }
}
```
kiyomi (Eng): For the migration note: call out v0.9 SDKs renamed `export_logs` -> `audit.export` (or similar). Add a table in the doc for quick 0.8->0.9 mapping.
jude (Legal): Approved the public wording after Zoe updates it. One legal caveat: clarify that redaction is irreversible for exported copies flagged `redacted=true` in the payload so customers understand compliance implications.
rick (Security): Also include guidance for large exports: prefer compressed streaming with checksums, set `page_size` conservatively, and use `page_token` restart rather than re-running entire job. Add example of resume flow.
zoe (Docs): Added a short resume snippet and a JSONL redaction example showing the `redacted` boolean: `{\"timestamp\":\"2026-07-01T08:00:00Z\",\"event\":\"access\",\"user_id\":\"acct_99\",\"redacted\":true}`. Updated PR copy to use Jude's phrasing and added a small "how to request purge" support link. Marking Jude and Rick as reviewers.
pavan (DevEx): Left Node and Python examples in the PR comments and a short troubleshooting bullet for checksum mismatches.
zoe (Docs): Thanks everyone — merging when CI is green. Will follow up in Release Notes with a pointer to the SDK migration guide and export checksum docs. :tada:
